cards.a: A protocol that carries PPP sessions over Ethernet, the standard for DSL/broadband. It uses PADI/PADO/PADR/PADS discovery to set up the session, then LCP/CHAP/IPCP run as usual.
It gives broadband Ethernet the authentication and addressing of PPP: per-subscriber sessions, PPP CHAP/PAP authentication, and IPCP addressing.

cards.q: What are the four PPPoE discovery messages in order?
cards.a: PADI (client broadcast), PADO (server offer), PADR (client requests), then PADS (session established). The session ID is issued by the access concentrator.

cards.q: What happens after PPPoE discovery completes?
cards.a: It behaves like classic PPP over a session: LCP configures the link, authentication runs via CHAP/PAP, IPCP assigns IP addressing, then data flows as PPP frames.

cards.q: What is the role of the access concentrator (AC/BNG) in PPPoE?
cards.a: It terminates PPPoE sessions, authenticates clients (often via RADIUS/CHAP), and routes them to the Internet.

cards.q: How is a PPPoE client configured on IOS-XE?
cards.a: Create a Dialer1 virtual interface with ip address negotiated, encapsulation ppp, dialer pool 1, ppp authentication chap callin, and bind the physical interface with pppoe enable and pppoe-client dial-pool-number 1.

cards.q: Which command links a PPPoE client's physical interface to the dialer pool?
cards.a: pppoe-client dial-pool-number 1 on the physical interface, combined with dialer pool on the Dialer interface.

cards.q: Which commands verify a PPPoE session?
cards.a: show ip interface dialer and show interface Dialer1 verify the interface; show pppoe session shows sessions; debug pppoe events troubleshoots discovery.

cards.q: Why is the MTU set to 1492 on a PPPoE link?
cards.a: Because of the 8-byte PPPoE header overhead, the effective MTU is reduced to 1492, so the link MTU should be set to 1492.

cards.q: A PPPoE client cannot establish a session. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: Discovery being blocked is the likely cause; check with show pppoe session and debug pppoe events.

cards.q: A PPPoE client authenticates but gets no IP address. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: An IPCP issue is likely; verify ip address negotiated is configured on the Dialer and debug ppp to see negotiation.

cards.q: PPPoE is slow with fragmentation. What is the likely cause and fix?
cards.a: MTU mismatch; adjust to mtu 1492 on the link to account for PPPoE overhead.

cards.q: What is the PPPoE session model when connecting a DSL subscriber?
cards.a: The Dialer interface hosts the virtual PPPoE session, the physical interface is bound via pppoe-client dial-pool-number, and authentication rides PPP (CHAP/PAP).
